baseline.common:
# Noctyx common exclusions — applied to every profile on every host.
#
# House rule: this list is deliberately SHORT. Excluding something is how data
# goes missing at 3 a.m., so every entry states why it is safe. Anything whose
# absence would be noticed is NOT here.

# ── Kernel/virtual filesystems: no content, often unreadable, always rebuilt ──
/proc
/proc/**
/sys
/sys/**
/dev
/run
/run/**
/tmp/**
/var/tmp/**
/var/run
/srv

# ── Rebuilt at boot / install time ──
/swapfile
/swap.img
/lost+found
/core
/var/lib/systemd/coredump/**
/var/crash/**

# ── Separate mount points. These are BACKUP SOURCES IN THEIR OWN RIGHT, not
#    part of this machine's root filesystem. Replaying them inside a root
#    restore would drop other people's archives onto a boot disk. ──
/mnt/**
/media/**
/autosrv
/ceph/**

# ── Snap/flatpak squashfs: re-downloadable, and the mounts are loop devices ──
/snap/**
/var/lib/snapd/cache/**
/var/lib/flatpak/exports/**
#    /var/lib/docker is NOT here: it is per-host policy (cluster.json backup_policy,
#    UI › Config). Default: /var/lib/docker/* excluded (image layers, container
#    rootfs — regenerable) and /var/lib/docker/volumes re-included (named volumes
#    hold real state: databases, app homes). Rendered into profile-*.d/exclusions.

# ── Package-manager download caches: re-fetched by apt on demand ──
/var/cache/apt/archives/**
/var/lib/apt/lists/**
/var/lib/apt/**

# ── Transient logs (journald archived). Keep /var/log itself — service logs
#    that matter belong in /var/log, and losing the whole tree would hurt. ──
/var/log/journal/**
/var/log/*.gz
/var/log/*.1
/var/log/*.old

# ── Network-mount contents that are somebody else's backup already ──
/**/noctyx-mount/**
/**/noctyx-mount/**

# ── Recursive garbage that breaks directory walks ──
/**/*.part
/**/*.filepart
/**/*.tmp

# ── Deliberately NOT excluded (recorded so nobody adds them later) ─────────
#  /etc            the whole point of a system backup
#  /boot, /boot/efi  bootloader + kernel + initrd. Often SEPARATE MOUNTS: the
#                  head deliberately does not use --one-file-system. Omitting
#                  /boot from a "full system backup" is the most dangerous single
#                  mistake available.
#  /root, /home, /opt, /var, /workspace  where the payload actually lives
#  /usr            small; "system dirs only" would skip almost everything real
#  dot-dirs and caches (~/.cache, /root/.cache, .npm, .conda, .triton, .nv,
#                  .cargo, .git/lfs): ~/.cache/huggingface/hub and git-lfs clones
#                  are where a cluster's LLM weights live, and "re-download it" is
#                  not a backup — models get pulled from the hub, gated or
#                  rewritten. Nodes sharing a repository store a shared model once.

# ── this site's own mount points (site config common_exclusions_extra) ──
/data/**

profiles.headdata:
# Noctyx exclusions for the head node's `headdata` profile (/storage, /mnt/scratch).
# Used INSTEAD of exclusions-common.conf: that list excludes /data/** and /mnt/**,
# which are exactly this profile's paths.
#
# Same house rule: every entry says why it is safe to lose.

# ── chain node data: re-syncable from the network, and a live node's LevelDB
#    copied file-by-file while it runs is not a consistent database anyway.
#    (The same list external-tool's backup-root.sh excluded.) ──
/data/app-code/data
/data/app-code/soak-store
/data/app-code/soak/verify-store
/data/core-oracle
/data/bench-tier3/ours
/data/chain-regtest/regtest
/data/chain-regtest2/regtest
/data/app-setinfo-scratch/h200k
/mnt/scratch/webapp-app/app/main

# ── Benchmark runs: ~1 TB each, a new one every day or two, regenerated by
#    re-running. Mirroring these without --delete filled nas (worklog 22). ──
/mnt/scratch/bench

# /data/*/.cache, qwen-vllm-cache and qwen-flashinfer-cache were excluded
# here until 2026-10-19; caches are backed up now (see exclusions-common.conf).
